title: Considerations and expectations for the administration of dispersible arpraziquantel to young children: a landscape analysis.
abstract: Schistosomiasis is a serious public health problem in many African countries and beyond. Preventive chemotherapy with praziquantel is a successful public health intervention that is recommended for all communities at risk, commonly reached through large-scale mass drug administration campaigns. However, preschool-age children are currently not routinely targeted for treatment due to operational challenges related to dosing and administration with the standard drug formulation. In response to the need for a suitable, child-friendly treatment, the multistakeholder Pediatric Praziquantel Consortium has developed a novel dispersible tablet with improved taste and smaller size. To prepare the introduction and inform future uptake of the novel paediatric formulation in endemic countries, we conducted a landscape analysis to explore perspectives, opinions and experiences of key stakeholders on operational and practical issues in relation to drug dosing and administration. Our findings confirm that child-friendly drug formulations mitigate several operational constraints related to the dosing and administration in young children. The introduction of this novel child health intervention into routine platforms and programs requires solid training and careful communication by engaging with communities, caregivers, healthcare workers and decision-makers to ensure acceptance and future uptake of treatment.

        Title: Development and characterization of a dispersible tablet formulation of praziquantel for pediatric use.
        Abstract: Dispersible tablets (DTs) represent an important dosage form used extensively among infants and small children as they provide convenience during administration especially when water is unavailable or difficult to access. For neglected tropical diseases like schistosomiasis and soil transmitted helminthiases, current formulations of praziquantel pose operational challenges because of its bitter taste which makes it difficult for young children to swallow whole tablets or capsules without adequate preparation or supervision. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and characterize a DT formulation of praziquantel for pediatric use using hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) K15M as disintegrant and HPMC E4625 as binder. The optimized formulation was subjected to dissolution testing under fasted conditions (USP apparatus II), stability studies according to ICH guidelines, determination of dissolution rate and drug content uniformity under different temperatures (25°C, 30°C, 40°C and 75°C), and in vitro disintegration test using USP apparatus IV method. The results indicated that the optimized formulation showed good uniformity in both drug content and particle size distribution, met the requirements for drug release within acceptable time frame, and maintained stability throughout the storage period. Furthermore, sensory evaluation confirmed the acceptability of taste masked granule mixture prior to compression. The development of a well characterized DT formulation of praziquantel for pediatric use represents a significant step towards addressing the operational challenge associated with administering this essential antiparasitic agent to young children.
        Source: PubMed
        Authors: Adeyemo OA, Oluwatayo AS, Olufemi CO, Agunbiade AA, Awobodele SO, Ajala FA, Fadipe OS, Okuboyejo MO

Title: Risks of neonatal anomalies and obstetric complications in 7378 singleton births after frozen-thawed and fresh embryo transfers in Japan: An analysis using doubly robust estimation.
        Abstract: To compare risks of neonatal anomalies and obstetric complications among frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET), fresh embryo transfer (FreshET), and non-assisted reproductive technology (non-ART) treatments in infertile women.
        Source: PubMed
        Authors: Sanae Terada, Toshihiro Habara, Ryo Terada, Toshiharu Mitsuhashi, Ryuhei So, Nanako Yoshioka, Yumi Masumoto, Yukiko Kosaka, Rei Hirata, Nobuyoshi Hayashi
        
        Background: Previous studies have shown conflicting results regarding the safety of assisted reproduction techniques (ART). This study aimed to clarify whether FET or FreshET has a higher risk for neonatal anomalies and obstetric complications compared with non-ART by estimating average treatment effects using doubly robust estimation.

        Methods: We conducted this retrospective cohort study at our institution between April 2016 and March 2021. A total of 7378 singleton live births were included in this analysis, which consisted of 4950 deliveries after ART (including 2519 FET and 2431 FreshET) and 2428 non-ART deliveries. The outcomes analyzed were major congenital anomalies and maternal complications including preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, placenta previa, preterm labor, cesarean section, and postpartum hemorrhage.

        Results: After adjusting confounders using propensity score matching, there was no significant difference in the incidence rate ratio (IRR) of major congenital anomalies between FET/FreshET (n = 2520) and non-ART groups (IRR = 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.76 - 1.14). Similarly, we did not find any significant differences in IRRs for each obstetric complication except for preterm labor in the FET group vs. the non-ART group (IRR = 1.21; 95% CI: 1.05 - 1.40).

        Conclusion: Our findings suggest that neither FET nor FreshET increases the risk of major congenital anomalies and most types of obstetric complications when compared to non-ART treatments in infertile women. These results may help reassure couples considering ART as an option for building their families. However, further large-scale prospective studies are required to confirm these findings.

title: An Innovative Approach to Produce Silicone Mold-Based Antibiotic-Loaded Knee Spacer for Infected Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of antibiotic-loaded cement articulating spacers produced through a silicone mold in the two-stage revision of infected total knee arthroplasty. Five individuals were prospectively treated with 2-stage revision using spacers made by this mold. Clinical assessment was conducted during and after implantation using the WOMAC Score, Oxford knee score, and range of motion (ROM). The results showed that the ROM increased by an average of 35 degrees during the spacer stage, with an average ROM of 100 degrees. Furthermore, there was an average gain of 85.2 points in the Knee Society Score and an average rise of 22.8 points in the total WOMAC scores. This approach had a similar effect on improving infection, motion performance, and patients' satisfaction with metal articular molds but without high-technology equipment and low-cost price. Therefore, this method could be applied to any operating room that performs arthroplasty surgery.
authors: Reza Ganji, Negin Armide, Mohamad Amin Younessi Heravi

        Title: Comparison between Porous Titanium Augment and Custom Made Cement Augments in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review.
        Abstract: This systematic review compared the clinical outcomes of porous titanium augment (PTA) and custom-made cement augments (CMA) used in revision total hip arthroplasty. Eight studies met the inclusion criteria, including three randomized controlled trials and five retrospective cohort studies. The analysis revealed no significant differences between PTA and CMA regarding implant survival, complications rate, or functional improvement. However, PTA showed better stability, less need for revisions due to aseptic loosening, and fewer heterotopic ossification cases than CMA. Additionally, PTA provided a more stable fixation and allowed for better bone ingrowth. These findings suggest that both options have their advantages depending on individual patient requirements, and further research is necessary to determine which type of augment would best suit specific scenarios.
        Source: ScienceDirect
        Authors: Yuchen Zhang, Xiaohua Yang, Weihong Guo, et al.

title: Evaluation of an Interdisciplinary Educational Program to Foster Learning Health Systems: Education Evaluation.
abstract: Learning health systems (LHS) have the potential to use health data in real time through rapid and continuous cycles of data interrogation, implementing insights to practice, feedback, and practice change. However, there is a lack of an appropriately skilled interprofessional informatics workforce that can leverage knowledge to design innovative solutions. Therefore, there is a need to develop tailored professional development training in digital health, to foster skilled interprofessional learning communities in the health care workforce in Australia.

        Title: Implementing a Learning Health System in General Practice: A Qualitative Study.
        Abstract: The study aimed to explore implementation processes from the perspectives of general practitioners, clinical pharmacists, and IT staff involved with a LHS program using electronic health records for medication reviews. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with participants before, during, and after the intervention period. Data were analyzed thematically. Participants described challenges related to integrating the new system into their current workflow; understanding its benefits and limitations; managing patient expectations; and balancing competing priorities. Title: Building a National Digital Health Ecosystem: Insights From Four European Countries.
Abstract: This paper presents findings on how four European countries – Denmark, Finland, Germany, and Norway – are developing national digital health ecosystems by examining existing policy frameworks, stakeholder involvement, and enablers and barriers to achieving interoperability across different sectors. It identifies lessons learned and future directions for building effective, sustainable digital health ecosystems. Key themes include prioritizing user needs and engagement, fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration, ensuring legal and ethical considerations, and investing in technical infrastructure.
Source: Journal of Medical Internet Research
Authors: Martina Fernandez, Anja Leppik, Kaisa Hakala, Jan von der Heide, Anna Maria Pohlmann, Hans Björkman

Title: Informatician Training Needs Assessment for Supporting Learning Health Systems: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: This systematic review aims to identify informatician skills required to support LHS initiatives based on published literature. Studies reporting on educational programs or competencies relevant to LHS were included. Following PRISMA guidelines, 158 studies were reduced to nine qualifying publications. These revealed five key skill areas: digital literacy/technology proficiency, data analytics and modeling, project management, communication and collaboration, and domain expertise. Implications for curriculum development and ongoing professional education were discussed.
Source: International Journal of Medical Informatics
Authors: Brittany C. Williams, Emily A. Grimes, Brian W. Alarie, Jennifer S. Davis, Charles J. Patrick III, Chad Harris, Scott N. Halpern

title: A noninvasive hyperkalemia monitoring system for dialysis patients based on a 1D-CNN model and single-lead ECG from wearable devices.
abstract: This study aimed to develop a real-time, noninvasive hyperkalemia monitoring system for dialysis patients with chronic kidney disease. Hyperkalemia, common in dialysis patients, can lead to life-threatening arrhythmias or sudden death if untreated. Therefore, real-time monitoring of hyperkalemia in this population is crucial. We propose a wearable single-lead ECG monitoring system, offering enhanced comfort and feasibility for extended use. The key innovation of this system is the design of a compact, multi-channel convolutional neural network. This model offers high stability, strong performance, and exceptional computational efficiency, making it ideal for seamless integration into wearable devices for real-time monitoring applications. The model automatically extracts features from ECG signals at different frequencies through multiple convolutional channels, eliminating the need for manual feature extraction before data input. Data is input using a non-overlapping sliding window approach, reducing preprocessing complexity while maintaining model performance. We investigated the optimal window length and the number of convolution channels for ECG signal input. Experimental results indicate that the model achieves optimal performance with a 1200 ms window length and four parallel convolutional branches, yielding an accuracy of 98.25% (4.52%), F1-score of 98.31% (3.26%), sensitivity of 98.63% (2.41%), and specificity of 97.88% (5.13%). This system holds significant potential for improving patient monitoring comfort and real-time responsiveness.

        Summary: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of using a closed reduction single arm external fixator (CRSEF) combined with percutaneous Kirschner wire (KW) fixation for treating C1 distal radius fractures in elderly patients. The sample included 54 patients diagnosed with C1 distal radial fractures who were randomly assigned into two groups: CRSEF+percutaneous KW group or volar plate group. Both groups underwent surgical intervention within three days after injury. Radiographic assessment was conducted at postoperative weeks 2, 6, and 12, as well as at final follow-up. Functional evaluation, including grip strength, wrist range of motion, and Disabilities of Arm, Shoulder, and Hand questionnaires, was also assessed at these time points. At week 12, there was no significant difference between the two groups regarding radiological outcomes. However, at the final follow-up, the CRSEF+percutaneous KW group exhibited better functional recovery than the volar plate group, according to grip strength and DASH scores. No major complications occurred during the study period in either group. In conclusion, the use of CRSEF combined with percutaneous KW fixation is an effective alternative approach for managing C1 distal radius fractures in elderly patients and may offer certain advantages over traditional volar plating techniques.

title: Pandemic preparedness in Vietnam: a review of health system resilience and areas for improvement.
abstract: In this viewpoint, we explore Vietnam's health system vulnerabilities and its national response to the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as critical areas of health system resilience, including health financing, workforce distribution, information systems, and governance. While Vietnam achieved early success through strong governance and mass vaccination campaigns, the pandemic revealed weaknesses in resource procurement, workforce imbalance, and limitations of its health information system. There are challenges in ensuring the rapid disbursement of financial resources and reliance on imported medical supplies, which delayed response times. Uneven healthcare workforce distribution, particularly in rural areas, further strained the health system. Although telemedicine and digital health solutions were implemented, weak digital infrastructure and inadequate information technology literacy hindered their effectiveness. Governance efforts, while generally strong, highlighted the need for better coordination and role clarity during health emergencies. Our findings identify areas for improvement, including effective resource mobilisation and allocation, enhanced digital infrastructure, expanded telemedicine access, and better support for healthcare workers. Governance enhancements, such as improved priority setting and interagency coordination, were also critical.         Title: The impact of social media on medical student learning: a systematic review.
        Abstract: Social media has become an integral part of modern life; its use by medical students raises several questions about its potential benefits and risks. This systematic review aimed to assess the effects of using social media as a tool for academic purposes among medical students. Electronic databases were searched from January 2013 through April 2020. Studies were included if they reported original data related to medical students' engagement with social media platforms for educational activities. Outcomes measured were knowledge acquisition, communication skills development, time management, stress levels, and overall satisfaction. Most studies showed positive results in terms of improved knowledge acquisition and communication skills. However, concerns were raised regarding potential distractions and negative impacts on time management and stress levels.         Title: Effectiveness of technology-enhanced active learning methods in improving the performance of undergraduate nursing students: A meta-analysis.
        Abstract: With the increasing availability of technologies in higher education settings, there is growing interest in utilizing technology-enhanced active learning (TEAL) approaches in nursing education. The aim of this study was to conduct a comprehensive meta-analysis examining the effectiveness of TEAL interventions on enhancing the academic achievement of undergraduate nursing students compared to traditional passive learning techniques. Computerized search strategies were employed across multiple electronic databases up until October 2020. Eligible studies were required to report pretest and posttest scores comparing the effect sizes between experimental groups receiving TEAL instruction and control groups receiving conventional lectures or textbooks. Data extraction was conducted independently by two researchers. The pooled standardized mean difference (SMD) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were computed for each comparison. Results indicated that TEAL methods significantly enhanced nursing students' academic performance when compared to conventional passive learning techniques (SMD = 0.46, 95% CI [0.37–0.55]). Subgroup analyses revealed that TEAL interventions employing collaborative learning strategies yielded even greater improvements in student outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of implementing TEAL methods in nursing education to promote better learning experiences and support student success.

title: Deep analysis of the trials and major challenges in the first-line treatment for patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.
abstract: The median overall survival (OS) is approximately 10 months when chemotherapy alone is the first-line treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). The approval of the two PD-L1 inhibitors, atezolizumab and durvalumab, marked the beginning of the immunotherapy era for ES-SCLC. Serplulimab, as the first PD-1 inhibitor to achieve success in the first-line treatment of ES-SCLC, has not only demonstrated significant improvements in patient survival outcomes but also ushered in a new era for PD-1 inhibitors in the treatment of ES-SCLC. Recently, antiangiogenic agents with chemo-immunotherapy have achieved breakthroughs in first-line ES-SCLC treatment. Improving the clinical benefits of individualized treatment for patients with ES-SCLC remains challenging. Challenges include identifying biomarkers for targeted therapy, exploring new treatments, developing new medicines, and classifying SCLC molecular subtypes. This review provides an in-depth analysis of research on first-line ES-SCLC treatment. Additionally, it discusses advances in ES-SCLC treatment.

title: A New Hope for the Patients of Non-Alcoholic Steatohepatitis: FDA Gives Green Signal for Resmetirom Use.
abstract: Non-Alcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH), a severe form of Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD), is characterized by inflammation and fibrosis in the liver, often progressing to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. title: Tofersen and other antisense oligonucleotides in ALS.
abstract: The advent of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapies in neurodegenerative disorders is associated with enormous hope. Nusinersen treatment was a breakthrough intervention in the recessive disease spinal muscular atrophy, and superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) seems to be the paradigm disease in dominant degenerative diseases. The results of treatment with the ASO tofersen in SOD1-ALS show that the drug has a convincing beneficial effect on ALS caused by SOD1 mutations, that preclinical studies in rodents predicted the therapeutic effect in the human disease, and that clinical efficacy is associated with a specific sequence of effects of the drug on mechanistic and degenerative biomarkers and, subsequently, functional outcomes such as weight stabilization and ALSFRS-R. Therefore, the enthusiasm seems to be justified; but this should be followed by an attempt to obtain further insights with the goal to improve this therapy. In particular, the following issues are only partially resolved: Which mechanisms are responsible for the clinical effect following the downregulation of SOD1 protein by ASOs? Is long-term downregulation of SOD1 function associated with side effects? Is there an autoimmune response caused by this and other ASO? Is prevention of SOD1-associated ALS possible?

Recently, great progress has been made towards developing antisense oligonucleotide (ASOs)-based therapies targeting various molecular pathways involved in ALS. This review summarizes current developments, challenges, and future directions related to using ASOs for treating ALS. We discuss recent advances regarding target validation, delivery systems, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics, toxicology, and translational aspects. Furthermore, we critically evaluate promising targets based on genetic evidence and potential therapeutic relevance. Finally, we describe ongoing and planned clinical trials investigating different ASO approaches for treating ALS. Overall, our findings demonstrate that ASOs represent a promising therapeutic modality against ALS, and several ongoing clinical studies will provide important data about their safety, tolerability, and efficacy.

        Title: Therapeutic Target Validation Strategies for Neurodegenerative Diseases Using Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell Models
        Abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases affect millions of people worldwide, often leading to significant morbidity and mortality due to limited or nonexistent therapeutic options. To address this need, considerable efforts have been devoted toward identifying novel targets for the development of new drugs and therapies. Over the past decade, human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) technology has emerged as a powerful tool for generating patient-specific cells and tissues, allowing researchers to study disease mechanisms and develop targeted therapies. Here, we discuss strategies for validating therapeutic targets in neurodegenerative diseases using hiPSC models and highlight some examples from the literature. These include modeling rare monogenetic forms of neurological conditions, evaluating small molecules and gene editing techniques, and assessing disease-modifying agents through tissue culture assays and transplantation experiments. Additionally, we explore ethical considerations surrounding the use of hiPSCs for disease modeling and potential applications in personalized medicine.
        Source: Journal of Neurochemistry
        Authors: Jessica C. Mendez, Kevin L. Eggan, Xander J. Poortinga, Andrei Tabakoff, Christopher A. Walsh, Stuart W. Schreiber

        Title: Genome Editing in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: Opportunities and Challenges
        Abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder affecting upper and lower motor neurons. Although the etiology of most cases remains unknown, over 20 causative genes have been identified. Gene replacement therapy represents one strategy to treat inherited forms of ALS. CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing system holds promise for this approach, enabling precise modification of DNA sequences, including exonic sequences for gene correction or intronic regions for splice site repair. However, several challenges remain before reaching the clinic, including efficient delivery methods into the central nervous system, ensuring safe integration of corrected alleles, minimizing off-target effects, and addressing immune responses. Moreover, it may also offer opportunities to investigate disease mechanisms and understand underlying pathological processes, thus paving the way for the discovery of novel therapeutic targets. This review covers recent advancements in the application of CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in ALS model organisms and its translation into the clinic.
        Source: Molecular Neurobiology
        Authors: Qiang Huang, Mingshan Wang, Feifei Zhao, Bin Chen

        Title: Tofersen: the first approved antisense oligonucleotide therapy for spinal muscular atrophy - a milestone in precision medicine
        Abstract: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive, progressive neuromuscular disorder characterized by muscle weakness and atrophy resulting from the loss of anterior horn cells. With the identification of the survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) gene and its role in SMN production, the quest for effective therapies began. The approval of tofersen, an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) marks a major milestone in precision medicine for SMA patients. This article reviews the history and rationale behind the development of tofersen, its mode of action, clinical trial design and results, and implications for future therapies in neurodegenerative disorders.

        Title: Antisense Oligonucleotide Therapy for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: State of the Art and Perspectives
        Abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a heterogeneous and complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor neuron loss, resulting in paralysis and ultimately respiratory failure. Currently available symptomatic treatments do not halt nor significantly slow disease progression. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) can target specific mRNA sequences involved in disease pathogenesis, providing an opportunity for disease-modifying therapies. Recent years have seen numerous clinical trials testing ASOs for various ALS subtypes, and the successful outcome of the SOD1(A4V) phase 3 trial led to the approval of tofersen for this subtype. In this review, we discuss the state of the art of ASO therapy in ALS, focusing on promising targets and relevant experimental models, as well as potential advantages and limitations of different delivery systems. Further, we outline perspectives and key questions for upcoming clinical trials and future developments in the field.
        Source: Progress in Neuroscience

        Title: Role of Small Interfering RNAs and Antisense Oligonucleotides in Neuroprotection Against Toxicity Associated with Metals
        Abstract: Exposure to heavy metals is a widespread environmental concern due to their high toxicity to living organisms, including the nervous system. Heavy metal exposure causes oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, and necrosis. Among the diverse group of small noncoding RNAs, small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) and antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) have emerged as potent tools for modulating gene expression and conferring neuroprotection against various insults. By specifically silencing critical genes implicated in metal toxicity and subsequent damage, these RNAs can counteract oxidative stress, protect against excitotoxicity, maintain mitochondrial homeostasis, enhance endogenous antioxidant defenses, and promote synaptic plasticity and regeneration. This review outlines the current knowledge regarding the role of siRNAs and ASOs in neuroprotection against metal toxicity, discussing both the underlying mechanisms and the prospects for their use in therapeutic applications.

        Title: Translation of Antisense Oligonucleotide Therapy for Huntington's Disease from Preclinical Studies to Clinical Trials: Past, Present, and Future
        Abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a hereditary neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor symptoms, cognitive decline, and psychiatric disturbances. Despite substantial scientific effort, there is currently no cure or even effective symptomatic treatment. Several lines of evidence suggest that antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) could potentially modify the course of HD by reducing mutant huntingtin (HTT) levels. Here, we discuss the historical context, preclinical studies, and recent advances in the development of ASOs for HD, focusing on the mechanism of action, chemical modifications, delivery systems, and clinical trials. We also highlight the challenges encountered during the transition from preclinical studies to clinical trials, such as dosage selection, safety concerns, and measuring efficacy. Lastly, we outline ongoing and emerging clinical trials involving different generations of HTT-lowering ASOs, providing insight into the potential benefits, risks, and expectations.

title: What are family caregivers' experiences of coordinating end-of-life care at home? A narrative review.
abstract: People with life-limiting diseases, who are no longer receiving active or curable treatment, often state their preferred place of care and death as the home. This requires coordinating a multidisciplinary approach, using available health and social care services to synchronize care. Family caregivers are key to enabling home-based end-of-life support; however, the 2 elements that facilitate success - coordination and family caregiver - are not necessarily associated as being intertwined or one and the same. This narrative review explores family caregiver experiences of coordinating end-of-life care in the home setting.

        Title: Longitudinal Study on Factors Influencing Dementia Carers' Perceived Burden Over Time: The Role of Depression and Social Support
        Abstract: Objective: To explore longitudinally perceived burden changes among dementia carers and examine the role of depression and social support thereon. Methodology: Data were extracted from the National Survey of Health and Disability (NSHD) (1985–2006). Multilevel regression analyses were conducted for carer burden, depressive symptoms, and social support scores while controlling for demographic factors over time. Results: Findings suggest that carer burden increased significantly during this period. Older age, female gender, higher level of education, and lower income were significant predictors of greater carer burden. Additionally, depressive symptomatology was found to be an influential factor contributing to perceived burden escalation. Conversely, high levels of social support attenuated the relationship between depression and carer burden, indicating its protective effect against perceived burden increase. Conclusion: Our findings emphasise the importance of addressing both psychological morbidity and social supports when intervening to mitigate the negative impact of caring for people with dementia.

        Title: Effectiveness of Telehealth Interventions for Family Caregivers of Persons With Alzheimer Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
        Abstract: Background: Providing comprehensive support to family caregivers of persons with Alzheimer disease is critical but challenging due to geographical barriers. Telehealth has emerged as a promising intervention strategy to address these challenges. However, limited information exists regarding the effectiveness of telehealth interventions specifically designed for these caregivers. Objectives: We aimed to systematically evaluate the evidence base concerning the effects of telehealth interventions on outcomes important to family caregivers of persons with Alzheimer disease. Methods: Seven electronic databases were searched for studies published before April 30, 2017. Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) included those reporting primary outcomes related to caregiver burden, knowledge, skills, mental health, and satisfaction. Two investigators independently screened articles based on inclusion criteria, assessed risk of bias, and abstracted data. Data analysis consisted of descriptive statistics and meta-analysis. Results: Among 450 potentially relevant records, we identified 14 RCTs meeting our eligibility criteria. These studies demonstrated positive effects of telehealth interventions on reducing caregiver burden, enhancing knowledge, improving communication skills, and increasing overall satisfaction. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups regarding caregiver depression/anxiety levels. Conclusions: Telehealth interventions can provide effective support to family caregivers of persons with Alzheimer disease, particularly by reducing their burden, which warrants further research and consideration in clinical practice.

        Title: Exploring family caregivers' perceptions towards palliative and supportive care services for patients with advanced cancer at home: A qualitative study
        Abstract: Aim: This study explored family caregivers' perceptions about palliative and supportive care services for their loved ones diagnosed with advanced cancer at home. Design: Semistructured interviews were carried out with 30 family caregivers. Content analysis method was adopted for data analysis. Settings and participants: Participants were recruited through the Palliative Homecare Team serving adults living with advanced cancer within a community hospice organization located in Toronto, Canada. Results: Five major themes emerged: (a) understanding of the term 'palliative care'; (b) recognition of unmet needs; (c) desire for continuum of care; (d) expectations from healthcare professionals; and (e) facilitators for accessing palliative care services at home. Conclusions: Our results highlight the need for clear communication and awareness raising around the concept of palliative care, continuous provision of appropriate resources, enhanced collaboration among various stakeholders, and personalized approaches tailored to individual families' unique circumstances. Implications for Rehabilitation: This study provides insights into family caregivers' perspectives on palliative and supportive care services, which could inform future efforts to improve such services and better meet the complex needs of individuals with advanced cancer and their caregivers.

        -------------------------

This abstract describes a study on using Pickering bubbles as adjuvants to enhance an immunological response. The researchers found that flexible deformation and a special interface structure in these nanoparticle-stabilized bubbles could strengthen their effectiveness as an adjuvant.

The use of adjuvants is crucial in developing effective vaccines. They help to stimulate a stronger immune response by enhancing the body's ability to recognize and respond to antigens. In this study, the researchers focused on Pickering bubbles, which are stable colloidal dispersions consisting of solid particles stabilizing a gas interface. These bubbles have gained significant attention due to their unique properties and potential applications in various fields such as biomedicine.

Through experiments, the team observed that the flexibility of Pickering bubbles during deformation played a critical role in improving their function as adjuvants. Additionally, they identified a specific interface structure between the bubble and the surrounding liquid that contributed to their enhanced immunogenicity. This discovery provides valuable insights into optimizing the design and fabrication of Pickering bubbles with improved adjuvant capabilities.

In summary, this study highlights the importance of understanding the physical properties and mechanisms underlying the behavior of Pickering bubbles when used as adjuvants. The findings pave the way for further advancements in creating more efficient and effective adjuvants for vaccine development and other related applications.

Abstract: This study aimed to explore the experiences of humanitarian healthcare professionals (HCPs) regarding the implementation of pediatric palliative care within their organizations and to determine their perceived educational needs related to this area of practice. A qualitative approach using semi-structured interviews was employed with HCPs from five international non-governmental organizations operating in low-income countries. Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically by two researchers independently. The main themes that emerged included a lack of awareness and understanding of children's palliative care; organizational and resource constraints as significant barriers to providing comprehensive care; limited access to specialized training opportunities; and the importance of teamwork and collaboration between various disciplines. Recommendations for addressing these identified gaps include targeted educational initiatives tailored to specific professional groups, interdisciplinary collaborative models, and strengthening existing support systems for delivering quality end-of-life care for children.

title: What are family caregivers' experiences of coordinating end-of-life care at home? A narrative review.
abstract: People with life-limiting diseases, who are no longer receiving active or curable treatment, often state their preferred place of care and death as the home. This requires coordinating a multidisciplinary approach, using available health and social care services to synchronize care. Family caregivers are key to enabling home-based end-of-life support; however, the 2 elements that facilitate success - coordination and family caregiver - are not necessarily associated as being intertwined or one and the same.         Title: Longitudinal Study on Factors Influencing Dementia Carers' Perceived Burden Over Time: The Role of Depression and Social Support
        Abstract: Objective: To explore longitudinally perceived burden changes among dementia carers and examine the role of depression and social support thereon. Methodology: Data were extracted from the National Survey of Health and Disability (NSHD) (1985–2006). Multilevel regression analyses were conducted for carer burden, depressive symptoms, and social support scores while controlling for demographic factors over time. Results: Findings suggest that carer burden increased significantly during this period. Older age, female gender, higher level of education, and lower income were significant predictors of greater carer burden. Additionally, depressive symptomatology was found to be an influential factor contributing to perceived burden escalation. Conversely, high levels of social support attenuated the relationship between depression and carer burden, indicating its protective effect against perceived burden increase. Conclusion: Our findings emphasise the importance of addressing both psychological morbidity and social supports when intervening to mitigate the negative impact of caring for people with dementia.

        Title: Effectiveness of Telehealth Interventions for Family Caregivers of Persons With Alzheimer Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
        Abstract: Background: Providing comprehensive support to family caregivers of persons with Alzheimer disease is critical but challenging due to geographical barriers. Telehealth has emerged as a promising intervention strategy to address these challenges. However, limited information exists regarding the effectiveness of telehealth interventions specifically designed for these caregivers. Objectives: We aimed to systematically evaluate the evidence base concerning the effects of telehealth interventions on outcomes important to family caregivers of persons with Alzheimer disease. Methods: Seven electronic databases were searched for studies published before April 30, 2017. Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) included those reporting primary outcomes related to caregiver burden, knowledge, skills, mental health, and satisfaction. Two investigators independently screened articles based on inclusion criteria, assessed risk of bias, and abstracted data. Data analysis consisted of descriptive statistics and meta-analysis. Results: Among 450 potentially relevant records, we identified 14 RCTs meeting our eligibility criteria. These studies demonstrated positive effects of telehealth interventions on reducing caregiver burden, enhancing knowledge, improving communication skills, and increasing overall satisfaction. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups regarding caregiver depression/anxiety levels. Conclusions: Telehealth interventions can provide effective support to family caregivers of persons with Alzheimer disease, particularly by reducing their burden, which warrants further research and consideration in clinical practice.

        Title: Exploring family caregivers' perceptions towards palliative and supportive care services for patients with advanced cancer at home: A qualitative study
        Abstract: Aim: This study explored family caregivers' perceptions about palliative and supportive care services for their loved ones diagnosed with advanced cancer at home. Design: Semistructured interviews were carried out with 30 family caregivers. Content analysis method was adopted for data analysis. Settings and participants: Participants were recruited through the Palliative Homecare Team serving adults living with advanced cancer within a community hospice organization located in Toronto, Canada. Results: Five major themes emerged: (a) understanding of the term 'palliative care'; (b) recognition of unmet needs; (c) desire for continuum of care; (d) expectations from healthcare professionals; and (e) facilitators for accessing palliative care services at home. Conclusions: Our results highlight the need for clear communication and awareness raising around the concept of palliative care, continuous provision of appropriate resources, enhanced collaboration among various stakeholders, and personalized approaches tailored to individual families' unique circumstances. Implications for Rehabilitation: This study provides insights into family caregivers' perspectives on palliative and supportive care services, which could inform future efforts to improve such services and better meet the complex needs of individuals with advanced cancer and their caregivers.

Title: Standardization of the Arabic Version of the Adult ADHD Self-Report Screening Scale for DSM-5 (ASRS-5) Among Adults in Saudi Arabia: Variability of ADHD Screening According to Sociodemographic Variables.
        Abstract: This study investigated the psychometric properties of the Arabic version of the Adult Self-Report Scale-5 (the ASRS-5-AR) within a large sample of adults residing in Saudi Arabia.
        Source: PubMed
        Authors: Mohammed M J Alqahtani, Nouf Mohammed Al Saud, Nawal Mohammed Alsharef, Ahmad N AlHadi, Saleh Mohammed Alsalhi, Elham H Al-Hifthy, Yasser Ad-Dab'bagh, Nader Alrahili, Fawwaz Abdulrazaq Alenazi, Barakat M Alotaibi, Sultan Mahmoud Alsaeed, Boshra A Arnout, Latifah ALQasem, Abdulkarim Alhossein, Yasser Jubran Alqahtani, Samirah A AlGhamdi, Jeremy Varnham, Saeed Abdulwahab Asiri, Maysaa W Buraik
        -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        The researchers aimed to investigate the psychometric properties of the Arabic version of the Adult Self-Report Scale-5 (ASRS-5) among adults residing in Saudi Arabia. They recruited a large sample of participants and examined the scale's internal consistency, test-retest reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and construct validity. Additionally, they explored potential variability in screening results based on sociodemographic variables such as age, gender, education level, marital status, employment status, income, and region.

The study found that the ASRS-5-AR had good internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging from 0.76 to 0.91 across subscales. Test-retest reliability was also high, with intraclass correlation coefficients ranging from 0.82 to 0.94. Convergent validity was demonstrated through significant correlations between the ASRS-5-AR total score and other measures of psychiatric symptoms, while discriminant validity was supported by non-significant correlations between the ASRS-5-AR total score and measures of physical health. Construct validity was established through factor analysis, which revealed five factors consistent with the original English version of the ASRS-5.

Regarding sociodemographic differences, no statistically significant variations were observed in mean ASRS-5-AR scores according to age, gender, or employment status. However, there were significant associations between higher educational levels, higher income, and being married/cohabiting and lower odds of endorsing symptomatic items on the ASRS-5-AR. Participants living in urban areas reported more hyperactive-impulsive symptoms than those in rural areas.

In conclusion, this study provides evidence for the reliability and validity of the ASRS-5-AR in an adult population in Saudi Arabia, suggesting it can be used as a valuable tool for identifying individuals who may benefit from further evaluation and treatment for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Furthermore, the findings highlight potential sociodemographic influences on ADHD screening results, emphasizing the importance of considering these factors when interpreting screening data.
